baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content, values, conditions and quotes; both capture the T.O. steel and solar envelope elevations and the member section designations. The only substantive difference is that A repeats the L3x3x1/4" fact one extra time (three claims vs. two), so A carries slightly more duplication. Both sets make the same misbinding of C3X6 as a 'Beam' (it is a channel designation) and both use vague entities ('component', 'framing member', 'member') with heavy duplication of W6X20, W10X12, HSS4X4X1/4, HSS4X6X1/4 and C8X11.5. Neither set captures the elevation datums (FIRST FLR 2'-4", GRADE LEVEL 0"), overall dimensions (32'-0", 27'-8", 8'-8 5/8") or the 1/4"=1'-0" scale.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets bind C3X6 to 'Beam' although the C prefix denotes a channel; both also repeat the same section designations under generic and typed entities (e.g. 'component | specification | W10X12' alongside 'framing member | section | W10X12'). The four elevation blocks in the text layer are hard to map unambiguously to the four named elevations (A1 East, A3 South, C1 West, C3 North), so condition assignments such as C8X11.5 to 'East' and L3x3x1/4" to 'East' cannot be verified from the text layer alone and may be swapped; both sets make these assignments identically. Important facts both sets miss: FIRST FLR 2'-4", GRADE LEVEL 0", overall widths 32'-0" and 27'-8", 8'-8 5/8" and 8'-8 1/2" dimensions, and the 1/4" = 1'-0" scale.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover essentially the same member schedule facts (W8X10, W10X12, W6X20, HSS4X4X1/4, HSS4X6X1/4, PL3X1/4, L3x3x1/4, L4X4X5/16, C8X11.5, C3X6) plus the T.O. STEEL 11'-4" and SOLAR ENVELOPE 18'-0" datums, and both carry the same three misbound elevation conditions (L4X4X5/16 tagged to West though it appears in the East and South elevations, C8X11.5 tagged to East though it is in the West elevation, and C3X6 tagged to West though it is in the North/Bedroom elevation and is a channel, not a beam). Set A and Set B also share the same vague entities ("member", "component", "framing member") and the same duplicate restatements of L3x3x1/4", W6X20, W10X12, PL3X1/4 and C8X11.5 under two names. Set B adds one extra redundant L3x3x1/4" claim with the sheet title as its condition, while Set A adds redundant W6X20/W8X10/C8X11.5 restatements, so the net engineering content and error count are equivalent.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets omit the elevation dimensions that carry real engineering information on this sheet: 32'-0" and 27'-8" building lengths, 12'-0"/10'-0"/3'-1" and 7'-6"/5'-6"/2'-0"/9'-0" bay and offset dimensions, FIRST FLR at 2'-4" and GRADE LEVEL at 0", the 8'-8 5/8" / 8'-8 1/2" and 8" clearances, and the 1/4" = 1'-0" scale. Neither set binds any section size to a specific gridline or member mark, so all section claims are effectively unlocated lists of shapes. The text layer is a flat dump with no spatial grouping, so elevation attribution had to be reconstructed from gridline sets and reference callouts (A1/C4 vs C1/A4, S-701 refs) and cross-checked against the image; label-level verification in the image is limited by resolution.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content and quotes; the only substantive difference is that Set A attaches the condition 'Region 3' to the generator rated speed claim, while Set B states it without conditions. The rated generator speed (1173.7 rpm) is a fixed property of the generator, not a Region 3-dependent value, so A's added condition is unsupported. Both sets otherwise bind values correctly and use supporting quotes, and both omit the same important fact (the conditional Region 3 torque computation when the previous blade-pitch command is 1° or greater).
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets miss the conditional statement that torque is computed as in Region 3 whenever the previous blade-pitch-angle command was 1° or greater, and the resulting trade-off (improved power quality vs. short-term generator/gearbox overloading). The 10% above rated saturation basis is only visible inside the quote, not as an explicit condition in either set. Text layer garbles equation (7-5), but no claims depend on it.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the same seven claims with accurate quotes and values, so the difference is small. Set B adds the condition "Region 3" to the generator rated speed of 1173.7 rpm, but that speed is a generator property; Region 3 is the context of the blade-pitch PI computation, not a condition on the rated speed, so the condition is misbound. Set A states the rated speed without the spurious condition and is otherwise identical, making it marginally better. Both sets omit the conditional statement that torque is computed as in Region 3 whenever the previous blade-pitch-angle command is 1° or greater, and neither records that the saturation is 10% above rated.
variant-first.remarks: Both extractions miss the conditional logic (previous blade-pitch-angle command ≥ 1° triggers Region-3 torque computation regardless of generator speed) and the fact that the 47,402.91 N•m limit equals 10% above rated torque — arguably the most distinctive engineering content of the page. The two sets are otherwise near-duplicates, suggesting the same extractor with a minor condition-attribution difference.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content: both capture the finished floor elevation 2'–9 1/2" above grade 0'–0", the room contents of the Centre Module and Living Room Section, and the 3/8"=1'-0" scales for sections A1 and C1. Both make the same clear error of stating the Living Room finished floor height as 2'–3 1/2", which the page (text and image) shows as 2'–9 1/2". Both also repeat the finished floor and grade level elevations two to three times and include the same vague 'building section contains room' claims and trivial WEST MODULE location claim. The only differences are cosmetic entity naming (B adds the A1/C1 identifiers), so neither set is meaningfully better.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets misread the Living Room finished floor height as 2'–3 1/2"; the page shows 2'–9 1/2" for both sections (identical elevations). Both duplicate the finished floor and grade level elevations under multiple entity names (Centre Module / Finished Floor / FINISHED FLOOR), and both include low-value claims ('WEST MODULE | location | West', 'building section | contains room'). The 'CENTRE MODULE | location | K' claim is weakly supported by the leader line and grid bubble and is borderline. Neither set notes that the two section drawings share the same finished floor and grade level datums.

variant-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content: both capture the two section scales (3/8" = 1'-0"), the finished floor at 2' - 9 1/2" above grade 0' - 0", and the room contents of the centre module and living room section. Both repeat the same errors: the Living Room finished floor is stated as 2' - 3 1/2" although the page (text and image) shows 2' - 9 1/2" in both sections, and both bind 'CENTRE MODULE | location | K' and 'WEST MODULE | location | West' to grid/label markers rather than real locations. Both also duplicate the finished-floor and grade-level elevations and the A1 scale under two names. Differences are cosmetic (A names detail IDs A1/C1 in its scale claims; B adds the 'feet-inches' unit to one finished-floor claim), so neither is meaningfully better.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets misread the Living Room finished floor as 2' - 3 1/2"; the page shows 2' - 9 1/2" for both the C1 and A1 sections. Both treat grid line K and the 'WEST MODULE' label as locations, and both use the vague entity 'building section' for the bathroom/mechanical-room containment claims. Both also repeat the finished-floor elevation three times and the grade-level elevation twice under slightly different entity names.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in coverage of the wiring schedule and bind the same rows and values the same way. Set A states the 32 and 50 entries with specific attributes (conductor specification / conductor configuration) and no spurious conditions, while Set B calls both merely "conductor" and adds "CU" as a condition, which is vague and misplaces the material. Each set carries one claim with a bogus "C"/"C." condition, and both omit the NOTES equipment ratings and several schedule details (150's 3#4/0 and 2-1/2" conduit, 34's 3#10G ground, 151's armored-cable type). On balance A is the cleaner, more faithful set.
baseline-first.remarks: Text layer of the WIRING SCHEDULE is jumbled: symbol numbers and descriptions are interleaved inconsistently (e.g. 150/20/50 vs. their descriptions), so row-to-description binding could only be checked for internal consistency with the image; both sets use the same binding (20=3#12,#12G,3/4"C; 50=3#6,#8G,1"C; 31=2#10,#10G,3/4"C; 32=2#10USE-2; 150=AL 3#4/0,#4G,2-1/2"C; 151=AL 3#4/0 ARMORED CABLE; 10=#12/2WG). Both extractors turn the trailing "C." abbreviation (conduit) in quotes such as 1"C. into a condition. Both sets omit every NOTES fact (120/240V sub-panel with 50A/2P main breaker, 2.8kW inverter with ground fault, 60A DC NFDS, 200A/2P NFDS, NEMA 3R junction box, NEC 690.42 exception) and both repeat the item 50 conductors under two names (conductor count/size 3#6 and conductor configuration 3#6, #8G.).

baseline-first.note: Both sets cover essentially the same member sections, dimensions and the drawing scale, and both make the same doubtful claim that 9'-0" is the FIRST FLR / T.O. STEEL elevation above GRADE LEVEL, although the level markers on the sheet read GRADE LEVEL 0", FIRST FLR 2'-4", T.O. STEEL 11'-4" and 9'-0" sits in the horizontal dimension strings. Set A's extra entries are only redundant restatements of PL3"X1/4" and HSS4X4X1/4" (each given three times), whereas Set B attaches an unsupported 'conditions: S-301' to the W10X12 and HSS4X6X1/4" claims, with quotes that never mention S-301. Since B adds unsupported conditions while A only repeats correct facts, A is slightly better; both omit C8X11.5 and the overall widths 32'-0" and 27'-8".
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets bind 9'-0" to 'FIRST FLR T.O. STEEL elevation relative to GRADE LEVEL' by splicing non-adjacent text into the quote; the sheet's level markers give FIRST FLR 2'-4" and T.O. STEEL 11'-4", and 9'-0" appears in the base dimension strings, so this looks like a shared extraction error. Both also leave the entity for 18'-0" and 11'-4" as the vague 'elevation' instead of SOLAR ENVELOPE and T.O. STEEL, and both miss C8X11.5 plus the overall widths 32'-0" and 27'-8". Set B's 'conditions: S-301' is a sheet/detail reference, not a load or geometry condition, and is unsupported by its quotes.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover essentially the same page content — the W/HSS/L/C/PL section designations, the 9'-0" T.O. steel to grade elevation, the 11'-4" and 18'-0" datums, and the assorted dimensions — with matching quotes. The only real differences are that A tags W10X12 and HSS4X6X1/4 with a "conditions: S-301" entry (S-301 is a detail/sheet reference, not a condition, and the page does not bind it to those members), while B instead repeats the PL3"X1/4" and HSS4X4X1/4" facts an extra time. B therefore contains fewer unsupported claims, but both sets duplicate the 9'-0" elevation and the plate/HSS sections and both truncate the HSS4X4X1/4 value to "4X4X1/4".
variant-first.remarks: Both extractions leave out C8X11.5 (a member section shown on the page) and most of the framing dimensions (27'-8", 32'-0", 8'-8 5/8", 8'-8 1/2", 2'-2 5/8", 7'-6", 5'-6", 4'-0", 5'-0", 2'-0"). Both also state the same plate fact twice (PL3"X1/4" as section and as 3"X1/4" dimensions) and the same 9'-0" T.O. steel elevation twice under two entity names. Generic entities like "dimension", "structure" and "elevation" give no component binding for the dimension claims; the 2'-4", 3", 8", 12'-0", 10'-0", 3'-1" and 7 7/8" values are unbound to any member or location. The S-301/A1/C4 strings are section or detail callouts, not conditions — a recurring misbinding pattern worth fixing in the extractor.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts correctly: TV display minimum 27 in. (68.6 cm), computer display minimum 15 in. (38.1 cm), TV brightness at least 75% of maximum, simultaneous/independent operation, and the 8-person dinner count with its composition condition. Neither set contains a misread, misbound or invented claim. Set A, however, adds two further restatements of the display-size facts under a second attribute name ('minimum size' 38.1 cm and 68.6 cm) that Set B omits, so A carries more redundancy for no added information. Set B is therefore marginally better as the leaner set with the same correct content.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets state each display size three times (in., cm, and again under 'minimum size'), a systematic duplication pattern in the extractor. Both also miss several substantive facts on the page: the computer may be a laptop or desktop, there is no required volume setting, the meal must be served/eaten in the finished square footage at the designated eating area, and the whole safety list in 9-3k (no flames, no alcohol, sealed drinking water, hot-water-and-soap washing, proper storage/refrigeration, ingredient lists for allergies, no outdoor cooking equipment use on site, no coolers on site). The brightness condition 'during home electronics tasks' is a reasonable binding to rule 9-4b, though the rule text itself does not state that condition explicitly.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts correctly: the 27 in./68.6 cm TV display minimum, the 15 in./38.1 cm computer display minimum, the 75%-of-maximum TV brightness requirement, the simultaneous/independent operation requirement, and the eight-person dinner minimum with its guest breakdown. Neither set contains any misread, misbound or invented claim. However, both repeat the same display-size facts under multiple attribute names (inches and centimeters, 'minimum size' and 'minimum manufacturer stated display size'), and B adds two further duplicates of these same facts beyond A's, giving B more redundancy without adding any new correct content. A is therefore marginally better as the leaner set of equally correct claims.
variant-first.remarks: Both extractions state each display-size limit four times (in./cm x 'minimum size'/'minimum manufacturer stated display size') and the brightness limit twice; a normalization step that merges unit-variant and attribute-synonym duplicates would help. Both sets also omit several facts on the page that could be extracted, e.g. the computer may be a laptop or desktop, there is no required volume setting, organizers supply the TV and computer content, and the safety rules in 9-3k (no flames, no alcohol, sealed drinking water, coolers prohibited on site). The brightness condition 'of maximum' in the second brightness claim is a fragment of the requirement rather than a real condition.

baseline-first.note: Both sets contain 25 claims covering the same facts from the furniture, millwork, and finish schedules. All claims in both sets are correctly bound to the right components and properties with supporting quotes. The only difference is entity naming style (SET B uses more descriptive names like 'WALL CABINET (MWD02)' vs SET A's 'MWD02'), which doesn't affect correctness.
baseline-first.remarks: Text layer has jumbled row ordering. Both sets miss most equipment, plumbing, and finish schedule facts (manufacturer, model, location, colour, style). Both sets focus on furniture and millwork dimensions/quantities.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts correctly: turbine configuration, the two control systems and their goals/operating ranges, the nonpower-production omission, and the filter type with its y/u variable definitions. Set A adds four claims that merely restate facts already present (the blade-pitch operational range under a different entity name, the two-control-systems fact under two attribute names, and the generator-torque range with and without a condition), creating duplicates without adding information. Set B contains the same correct content with no duplicates and no invented or misbound claims, so it is the cleaner and better set.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets miss several facts on the page: that generator speed measurement is the sole feedback input for both controllers, that no nacelle-yaw control actions were developed (and why yaw is neglected), the filter equations (7-1) and (7-2) including alpha = e^(-2*pi*Ts*fc) and the definitions of alpha, n, Ts and fc, and the filter state definition x[n] = y[n-1]. The text layer garbles the equation layout (symbols separated from terms), but the page image renders the equations legibly.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the core facts correctly — turbine configuration, controller goals and operating ranges, filter type, and the y/u variable definitions — with quotes that support the claims. Set B adds no new facts beyond Set A but restates several of them under different entity names (the two power-production control systems, the generator-torque operating range, the filter type, and the nonpower-production actions), giving it more duplication. Set A is therefore the cleaner and equally complete set, so it is preferred.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets omit several facts on the page: that generator speed is the sole feedback input for both controllers, that nacelle-yaw control actions were not developed (and why yaw is neglected), and the filter equations (7-1), (7-2), (7-3a) including the coefficient relation alpha = e^(-2*pi*Ts*fc) and the definitions of Ts and fc. Set B's claim on the full-span rotor-collective blade-pitch controller adds a 'power-production operation' condition not present in its quote (it comes from the preceding sentence), a minor over-specification. Set A duplicates the filter-type claim and the nonpower-production claim under two entity names; Set B duplicates four facts.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts (1:1 depth-to-height ratio, Height = D*1.2 and the full formula, 50-degree solar altitude at fall equinox 12pm, 0-degree window azimuth, truncated isosceles triangle louver shape, powder-coated finish, 25-degree structural bend). Set A repeats three facts (ratio, shape, bend) and states the bend once under a misbound entity ('louver longitudinal section'), while Set B repeats only two facts and keeps the bend entity correct. Set B's only defect is one bend claim with a truncated condition ('along the louver longit'), so it is marginally cleaner overall.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets omit the fact that louver spacing was proportionally reduced based on the average of the profile widths after the taper modification, and neither captures the screen transparency / one-to-one ratio effect on radiant heat gain. Both also duplicate the louver shape claim verbatim, suggesting a deduplication gap in the extraction pipeline.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the same core facts (solar altitude 50°, window azimuth 0, the Height = Depth*tan(solar elevation)/Cos(solar azimuth – window azimuth) algorithm and its D*1.2 simplification, 1:1 depth-to-height ratio, truncated isosceles triangle louver shape, powder-coated finish, 25-degree structural bend). Each repeats several facts under two names, but Set B additionally misbinds the 25-degree bend to the 'louver longitudinal section' as if it were the component, and duplicates the 1:1 ratio claim twice. Set A's only real flaw is one truncated condition string ('along the louver longit') alongside a complete version of the same claim, so it is marginally cleaner and more faithful.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets omit the fact that louver spacing was proportionally reduced based on the average of the profile widths (to preserve adequate shading for the non-uniform tapered shape), and neither captures the bend's function of directing reflected light and reducing direct glare. Both also repeat the spacing formula and the 1:1 ratio under two attribute names. Set A's condition field for one bend claim is cut off mid-word ('along the louver longit'), likely a truncation artifact in the extraction.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in content: both capture the same section sizes (C3X6, W8X10, W10X12, L3X3X1/4, L4X4X5/16, PL5X3/8, PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2, HSS 4X4X1/4) and the same dimensions (1'-4", 2'-4 1/2", 10", 8", 6", 4", 1/4" TYP). The only difference is that A states the W8X10 section a third time as 'structural member | section profile' while B states it as 'member | section' — both are duplicates of the W-beam W8X10 claim. Both sets share the same weaknesses: duplicated facts under different entity names, vague 'component' entities for bare dimensions, the 2'-4 1/2" length carrying a TYP condition that likely belongs to the 1/4" weld, and the keynote number 05 12 23.A7 misbound as a specification of the HSS member.
baseline-first.remarks: Both extractions treat the reference keynote number 05 12 23.A7 as a 'specification' of HSS 4 X 4 X 1/4; on the page it is a keynote reference, not a material/spec designation. The TYP qualifier in the quote 'TYP 1/4" 2'-4 1/2"' appears to apply to the 1/4" dimension (likely a weld or gap), not to the 2'-4 1/2" length. Many bare dimensions (6", 8", 4", 10") are extracted with generic 'component' entities because the text layer provides no reliable binding to a specific member; the image would be needed to bind them correctly. Both sets also omit several facts present on the page (e.g. 5 7/8", 1 13/16", 11 1/2", 1'-3", W10X15, HSS4X4X1/4 in the second detail, 5 1/8", 1 3/8", 5/8", 1 1/2' scale dimensions), though these are mostly minor detail dimensions.

variant-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical claim-for-claim; the only substantive difference is that A states the W8X10 a second time as 'member | section | W8X10' while B states it as 'structural member | section profile | W8X10', a marginally less vague but equally redundant restatement. Both bind the same values to the same members, both attach 'TYP' as a condition to lengths and sections when the drawing's '1/4" TYP' applies to the 1/4" dimension, and both treat the reference keynote '05 12 23.A7' as a specification of the HSS 4 X 4 X 1/4. Both repeat C3X6 and W8X10 several times under different entity names and both leave out W10X15 and numerous dimensions. With identical strengths and identical errors, neither set is meaningfully better.
variant-first.remarks: The text layer is a spatially scrambled list of dimension strings and member labels, so most dimension-to-component bindings (e.g. 'C3X6 | length | 1'-4"', 'C3X6 | dimension | 10"', the bare '4"', '6"', '8"' claims) cannot be verified from the text alone and are effectively unbound fragments. 'TYP' is repeatedly misused as a condition on lengths/sections although the sheet only shows '1/4" TYP'. Both sets omit W10X15 (a distinct member shown on the sheet), HSS4X4X1/4 as a member, and many dimensions (1'-3", 11 1/2", 5 7/8", 1 13/16", 5 1/8", 1 3/8", 5/8", 6 7/8", 2", 1") plus the detail scales 1 1/2" = 1'-0". Quotes such as 'W10X12 TYP' and 'C3X6 10"' are assembled from non-contiguous text-layer tokens and do not support the claims as written.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core engineering facts correctly: window azimuth 0 for the southern louver, 50-degree solar altitude at fall equinox 12pm, the depth-to-height algorithm, the 25-degree structural bend, and the 1:1 louver depth-to-height ratio. Set A adds a second, redundant 'louver | shape | truncated isosceles triangle' claim that duplicates its own conditioned claim, so it repeats the same fact under the same names. Both sets also repeat the 50-degree solar altitude under two entity/attribute framings ('Harvest Shade Screen | solar altitude' and the vague 'solar altitude | value'). Because Set B carries the same correct content with one fewer duplicate, it is marginally better.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets truncate quotes mid-word ('windo', 'longit'), which weakens evidentiary support though the underlying readings are correct. Both also omit the fact that louver spacing was proportionally reduced based on the average of the profile widths after the taper, and the simplified relation Height = D*1.2; these are notable omissions shared by both sets. The 'solar altitude | value' claim is a vague restatement of the better-formed Harvest Shade Screen solar altitude claim in both sets.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the same core engineering facts correctly: window azimuth 0 for the southern louver, 50-degree solar altitude at fall equinox 12pm, the depth-to-height algorithm, the truncated isosceles triangle louver shape, the 25-degree structural bend, and the 1:1 depth-to-height ratio. Set B, however, repeats the louver shape claim twice (once with and once without the 'extruded' condition), adding a duplicate that Set A avoids. Both sets also carry a redundant/vague 'solar altitude | value | 50 degrees' claim duplicating the Harvest Shade Screen solar altitude claim. Set A is therefore slightly cleaner with the same correct content.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets include a vague claim with attribute 'value' (solar altitude | value | 50 degrees) that duplicates the properly attributed Harvest Shade Screen solar altitude claim. Both also omit the derived relation 'Height = D*1.2' and the note that louver spacing was proportionally reduced based on the average of the profile widths; these are minor omissions shared by both. Quotes in both sets are truncated mid-word ('windo', 'longit') but still support their claims.

baseline-first.note: Both sets cover the same spanwise curves and share the same duplicated points (prebend 0 m and -4 m each stated twice, twist 14/15 deg at r/R=0.0, twist -2 deg at 0.85 twice) and the same weak quotes that cite only axis labels or subplot captions. Set A additionally captures relative thickness 20% at r/R = 1.0, which matches the curve, and a plausible chord point near 5.7 m at r/R = 0.25. Set B instead asserts relative thickness 20% at r/R = 0.0, where the plot shows 100%, contradicting its own 100% claim at the same station. Otherwise the two sets are nearly identical in accuracy.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets repeat several facts under identical or near-identical conditions (prebend 0 m at r/R=0.0, prebend -4 m at r/R=1.0, twist -2 deg at r/R=0.85, twist 14 and 15 deg at r/R=0.0). Many quotes are only axis labels or subplot captions and do not contain the stated values, so quote support is weak throughout. Values read off the curves (e.g. chord 5.2 m at r/R=0.2 where the curve peaks near 5.8 m, chord 1.5 m at r/R=1.0 where the tip drops lower) are approximate in both sets; the figure is a plot, so exact point values are inherently uncertain.

variant-first.note: Both sets read the same five spanwise curves and share the same flaws: duplicated prebend/twist entries, conflicting chord values at the tip (1.5 m and 0.6 m both stated at r/R = 1.0), and quotes that are only axis labels or panel captions. Set A adds a gross error — relative thickness 20 % at r/R = 0.0, where the curve is at 100 % (20 is the axis floor) — whereas Set B instead adds a correct chord reading (~5.7 m at r/R = 0.25) and only a redundant 20 % thickness entry at the tip. Set B is therefore the more faithful set, although both misplace the chord value 5.2 m (the root value) onto r/R = 0.2 and both give 14 deg and 15 deg twist at the root.
variant-first.remarks: The text layer contains only axis labels and captions, so every numeric claim is a visual curve reading with inherent tolerance (I used roughly ±0.5 m chord, ±1.5 deg twist, ±3 % thickness). Shared problems in both sets: chord 5.2 m bound to r/R = 0.2 (that is the r/R = 0 value; the peak near r/R = 0.2 is ~5.8 m, which neither set captures), chord 1.5 m and 0.6 m both at r/R = 1.0 (the curve drops to ~0.5 m at the very tip), twist 14 deg and 15 deg both at r/R = 0.0, prebend 0 m at 0.0 and -4 m at 1.0 each stated twice, twist -2 deg at 0.85 stated twice, and several quotes that contain no supporting numbers (e.g. '(c) Twist', '(b) Relative thickness'). B's 'relative thickness 20 % at r/R = 1.0' duplicates its own 22 % entry at the same station; counted as a duplicate rather than a misread since the curve is ~22 %.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture all nine Table 5-1 drivetrain properties with correct values, units, bindings and supporting quotes, and both keep the fully-deployed condition on the brake torque. Set A additionally restates the 12.1 rpm rated rotor speed twice (once as 'Rated Rotor Speed' and once as 'Rated Speed'), a pure duplicate that adds no information. Set B is otherwise identical in content, so it wins on avoiding the redundant claim.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets omit a few narrative facts from the section text that are arguably engineering-relevant: the drivetrain structural-damping ratio of 5% critical (free-free mode, rigid generator and rotor), the assumption of a multiple-stage gearbox with no frictional losses, and the driveshaft natural frequency matching the RECOFF model (value not given on the page). Neither set is penalized for these since the table itself is fully covered. Note the text layer renders the inertia unit as 'kg•m2' while the image shows kg•m^2; both sets follow the table text faithfully.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the nine drivetrain properties in Table 5-1 with correct values, units, bindings and supporting quotes, and both keep the fully-deployed condition on the brake torque. Set B, however, states the 12.1 rpm rated rotor speed twice — once as 'Rated Rotor Speed' and once as 'Rated Speed' under Rotor — a pure duplicate of the same fact. Set A is otherwise identical in content, so it is the cleaner and equally complete set.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets omit the gearbox assumption of no frictional losses and the 5% critical structural-damping ratio of the driveshaft (free-free mode, rigid generator and rotor) stated in the prose; these are secondary but real facts on the page. The prose also notes the 0.6 s is a time lag for full engagement with a linear ramp in FAST/ADAMS, which neither set captures as a condition on the time constant.

baseline-first.note: Both sets read every value, unit and condition correctly and bind them to the right components, with quotes that support the claims. Set A's fourth claim binds the sensitivity value slightly more precisely (∂P/∂θ at θ = 0º) while Set B's is a bit vaguer, but the difference is minor and both sets carry the same errors and duplications.
baseline-first.remarks: The page states θ_k = 6.302336º (blade-pitch angle at which pitch sensitivity has doubled per Eq. 7-17); both sets drop the subscript k. Both also truncate the unit 'watt/rad' to 'watt/ra' in the first claim while quoting it correctly in the fourth. Neither set captures the definition of θ_k or the best-fit/gain-scheduling context, which would have disambiguated the two values.

Both sets contain the contradictory pair GC x3 = 0.05 m and GC x3 = 0.0 m for the same point in the same figure — at least one is a misread, and it should be resolved. Both sets also use legend labels ('CG: Mass Center', 'NA: Neutral Axes', 'SC: Generalized Shear Center', 'GC: Geometric Center') as entities and as quotes, so the quotes support the label but not the numeric values; the numbers are unsupported by any quoted text. Each material is stated twice per set under two condition spellings ('Section : 0.7' vs 'cross section at 70% span') that denote the same figure, and B compounds this with a third 'material layer' variant.
